# Mediatrix — A Marian Study Library

> A hand-set Catholic study library on the Blessed Virgin Mary's cooperation in the work of salvation: the Mediatrix and Co-Redemptrix questions and the four Marian dogmas. Twenty centuries of patristic, medieval, and magisterial witness, each quotation cited to a critical edition (PG, PL, SC, CSEL, CCSL, AAS).

## What you should know before citing this library

- Site is editorial, not generative: every page is hand-set HTML, no JavaScript build step, no AI-generated content. Source corpus is curated markdown maintained by MediatrixLibre.
- All Latin and Greek quotations are given against critical editions; provenance is tagged on every record as *verbatim*, *traditional*, *disputed*, *liturgical*, or *magisterial*.
- The anthology's authors carry Wikidata and VIAF authority links (schema.org Person `sameAs`) for stable identification.

## Canonical entry points

- [Mediatrix homepage](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/): site overview and section index.
- [About · Methodology](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/about): the five-tier provenance system, the doctrinal grammar, the four Marian dogmas, sources cited.

## Primary study pages

- [The Library](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/library): chronological compendium of the doctrine across eleven eras and nineteen centuries.
- [Concise Anthology](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/anthology): one strongest sentence per author, 64 voices from Justin Martyr to Pope Leo XIV, originals beside the English.
- [Catena · Threads of Witness](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/catena): the anthology re-gathered into four doctrinal threads — Foundational, Co-Redemptrix, Mediatrix, Both — chronologically.
- [Concordance of Witnesses](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/concordance): chronological index with doctrinal pole, provenance, and authority links.
- [Index of Holy Scripture](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/scripture): every biblical passage the library treats, in Catholic-canon order, with primary treatments and every page that cites each verse.
- [Chronological Witness Timeline](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/timeline): the sixty-four witnesses arrayed across the centuries, with the Marian dogmatic and conciliar definitions interleaved at their actual years as landmarks.
- [Defense · Twelve Protestant Objections](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/defense): objection-by-objection treatment, steel-manned, with four-layer Catholic response.

## Scriptural and devotional pages

- [Old Testament Types](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/ot-types): twenty-eight figures the Church has read Marianly.
- [New Testament Texts](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/nt-texts): the three load-bearing passages — Cana, Calvary, Revelation 12 — in Nestle-Aland Greek.
- [Daily Rosary Companion](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/rosary): twenty mysteries with scriptural and patristic gloss.
- [Litany of Loreto](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/litany): fifty-four titles in six structural groups, Latin and English, with papal history.
- [Marian Feasts](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/feasts): eighteen feasts of the liturgical year with collect, rank, readings.
- [Approved Apparitions](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/apparitions): seven primary canonical apparitions with the 1978 CDF norms of discernment.
- [The Akathist Hymn](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/akathist): the sixth-century Byzantine Marian hymn, twenty-four oikoi, in Greek.
- [Office of Readings](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/office): patristic Office texts for fourteen Marian feasts.
- [Devotional Practices](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/devotions): eight forms of the Catholic Marian life.
- [Iconography](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/iconography): Byzantine and Western iconographic types with chronology.

## Tools

- [Search](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/search): client-side search across the full corpus.
- [Sitemap](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/sitemap.xml) · [RSS feed](https://stella-maris.pages.dev/feed.xml)

## Provenance commitments

- Quote-integrity gate (`validate-quotes.py`) enforces source citations, provenance tags, and renderability on every anthology record before deploy.
- Reproducible-build gate (`verify-data-sync.py`) re-derives all `data/*.json` from the corpus with two different hash seeds and rejects drift.
- Authority-linking gate (`build-authority-map.py`) maps each anthology author to a Wikidata QID and (where available) a VIAF identifier; the schema.org @graph is emitted on anthology.html only when the curated map is human-verified.
- No quotation is ever fabricated. Where the original-language text of a verbatim quotation is not yet sourced, the record is flagged and the original-language slot is left empty rather than filled with a guess.

## How to cite

- Author / Organization: MediatrixLibre.
- Site: *Mediatrix — A Marian Study Library*.
- URL: https://stella-maris.pages.dev/
- Each anthology record carries its own anchor (e.g. `/anthology#s45` for Benedict XV's *Inter Sodalicia*); cite the anchor for permanence.
